default.headline: The campaign continues.
paragraphs: Your orders still carry weight — for now.

1.headline: The first command continues.
paragraphs: The record is still being written. Every match is evidence the next King will read.

2.headline: The second command continues.
paragraphs: They have heard about you; the rest of the campaign decides what they conclude.

3.headline: The final command continues.
paragraphs: There is no fourth King. Whatever this campaign becomes is the ending.

default.headline: Outplayed.
paragraphs: The roster marched where you pointed, but the positions you chose were losing. The pieces are spent, not shattered: they followed you into defeat.

1.headline: Outplayed in the first command.
paragraphs: They followed you into a losing position and held formation to the end. The failure was on the board, not in the room — which makes it the kind that can be learned from.

2.headline: Outplayed in the second command.
paragraphs: A roster that heard stories about you followed anyway, and lost. Loyalty carried them into your bad positions. That is a debt, not a compliment.

3.headline: Outplayed at the last command.
paragraphs: The final King watched his army follow you into checkmate. The career closes in defeat, but in an ordered one — they never stopped executing your orders.

default.headline: Dismissed.
paragraphs: The roster survives intact and still wants the win — they lost faith in your judgment, not in the mission. The King took the field; the debrief will show whether the army played better under a worse tactician who was obeyed.

lost_room.headline: You lost the room.
paragraphs: Under the King — a shallower tactician with an unspent mandate — the army played better than it did under you. The orders were worse and the results were better. That inversion is the whole lesson: your judgment was never the bottleneck. Your standing was.

broke_roster.headline: You broke the roster.
paragraphs: The King took the field and failed too. This is the worse ending: you did not merely lose command, you left a room no one could command. The ruins are the report.

1.headline: Dismissed from the first command.
paragraphs: Two Kings remain who have not yet refused you. What this roster reports about you will be waiting at the next court.

2.headline: Dismissed from the second command.
paragraphs: One King left. The next room will arrive knowing exactly how this one ended.

3.headline: Dismissed at the last command.
paragraphs: No King will start a match with you again. The career ends here — not with checkmate, but with a room that chose its King over you.

default.headline: Rout.
paragraphs: The army shattered. Desertion cascaded until only the King remained. This is the worst ending: not merely outplayed, but abandoned.

1.headline: Rout in the first command.
paragraphs: They did not wait to learn what kind of commander you would become. The desertion was the review — early, unanimous, and irreversible.

2.headline: Rout in the second command.
paragraphs: The room that had heard everything about you decided the rumors were true. A cascade this fast is never about one order; it is the accumulated record, priced.

3.headline: Rout at the last command.
paragraphs: The final army walked. There is no King left to appoint you, and no roster left to follow anyone. The career ends the way routs always end — alone, on a full board.

default.headline: Victory.
paragraphs: The army's realized play sustained above your personal ceiling — the roster executed well enough that the positions themselves carried the campaign. You led beyond your own tactical limit.

1.headline: Victory in the first command.
paragraphs: A new roster outplayed its own commander. The next King will hear of this — and will hold you to it.

2.headline: Victory in the second command.
paragraphs: Twice now the army has outrun its orders. The pattern stops being luck and starts being a reputation — the kind that precedes you into the last appointment.

3.headline: Victory at the last command.
paragraphs: The career closes with a roster that became more than the hand that led it. That is the only completion certificate this game issues.
